APPENDIX A – CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Official Product Name:
“Will an alternative wage for Californian goat herders be authorized <time period>?”
Rulebook:
CAGOATWAGE
CAGOATWAGE
Scope:
These rules shall apply to this contract.
Underlying:
The Underlying for this Contract is official records of the State of California and reporting from the Source

Agencies regarding legislative, regulatory, executive, and judicial actions affecting the minimum wage and overtime

obligations applicable to California employers of goat herders <time period>. Revisions to the Underlying made after

Expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.
Source Agency:
The Source Agencies are, in hierarchical order, California Legislative Information, the official journals of

the Assembly and Senate of California, the Office of the Governor of California, the California Secretary of State, the

California Department of Industrial Relations (including the Labor Commissioner/DLSE and the Industrial Welfare

Commission), the California Office of Administrative Law, the Official Californian Code of Regulations. the issuing court,

the Associated Press, Reuters, The Guardian, Bloomberg News, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The

Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, the San Francisco Chronicle, the Sacramento Bee, CalMatters, Politico, Axios,

CNN, ABC, CBS, NBC, Agri-Pulse, and Fox News.
Type:
The type of Contract is an Event Contract.
Issuance:
After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will be listed on an as-needed basis at the discretion of the Exchange

and corresponding to the risk management needs of Members.
<time period>:
<time period> refers to a specific duration or range of time as specified by the Exchange. May be

expressed as a calendar year (e.g., "2026"), a calendar month and year (e.g., "September 2026"), a calendar quarter (e.g., "Q3

2026"), a specific week, or other bounded time periods as appropriate to the contract subject matter. All time periods are

interpreted in Eastern Time (ET) unless otherwise specified. The end of <time period> is defined as 11:59:59 PM ET on the

final day of the specified period, unless otherwise specified. The Exchange may list iterations of the Contract corresponding

to variations of <time period>.
Payout Criterion:
The Payout Criterion for the Contract encompasses the Expiration Values that a Qualifying Action has

been taken <time period>.
A "Qualifying Action" means:
1.
a California statute has become law, whether by the Governor's signature, by passage over a gubernatorial veto under

Article IV, Section 10(a) of the California Constitution, or by operation of Article IV, Section 10(b), and regardless of

vehicle, including a policy bill, urgency statute, budget bill, budget trailer bill, or special session bill;
2.
a regulation finally approved by the California Office of Administrative Law and filed with the California Secretary of

State, or an Industrial Welfare Commission wage order that has been amended or republished and has taken effect;
3.
a written regulation, binding directive, final order, or formal statewide enforcement policy issued by a California state

agency, department, board, commission, or officer with authority over the subject matter, including but not limited to

the Department of Industrial Relations, the Labor Commissioner and the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement,

the Industrial Welfare Commission, the Employment Development Department, the Department of Food and

Agriculture, the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, and the Department of Finance. An opinion letter or

official interpretation is included only if it binds the issuing body or expressly states that body's statewide enforcement

position;
4.
an executive order or proclamation issued by the Governor of California; or
5.
a written order entered by a California state court or a United States federal court.

[page 2 of 5: text layer]
Which has at least one of the following effects:
1.
it reenacts, revives, restores, or extends the alternative monthly wage authority formerly contained in California

Labor Code Section 2695.4(a), or establishes an alternative to it;
a.
"Goat herder" means an individual employed to perform any of the duties described in former California

Labor Code Section 2695.3(d), as that section read immediately before its repeal on July 1, 2026. Where

an instrument described above defines goat herders or a comparable class differently, that instrument's

definition governs for purposes of applying the Payout Criterion to that instrument.
2.
it provides that goat herders are eligible for the alternative monthly wage framework applicable to sheepherders

under California Labor Code Sections 2695.1 and 2695.2, including by determining that "sheepherder" as used

in California Labor Code Section 2695.2 encompasses goat herders;
3.
it establishes an alternative monthly wage, a special minimum wage, a modified overtime threshold, a modified

compensable-hours rule, an exemption in whole or in part from minimum wage or overtime requirements, a safe

harbor, or a limitation on damages or penalties (subject to the conditions set out in what would NOT satisfy the

Payout Criterion), in each case applicable to goat herders or their employers;
4.
it directs that any portion of the minimum wage or overtime obligations otherwise applicable to California

employers of goat herders not be enforced or collected, including by a formal written policy of enforcement

forbearance;
5.
it provides employers of goat herders a tax credit, reimbursement, grant, subsidy, payment, or contract price

adjustment expressly tied to goat herder minimum wage or overtime obligations; or
6.
it enjoins or prohibits the enforcement or collection of any portion of the minimum wage or overtime

obligations otherwise applicable to California employers of goat herders, or declares those obligations wholly or

partially inapplicable to goat herders. A stay entered solely on procedural grounds, including arbitration, venue,

discovery, bankruptcy, or case management, is not a Qualifying Action unless the order itself bars enforcement

or collection of the underlying wage or overtime obligation.
And which:
1.
applies statewide, or is generally available to employers of goat herders as a class, and is not limited to a named

employer, a named individual, or the parties to an individual, non-class case;
2.
was enacted, approved and filed, issued, or entered, as applicable, on or before the end of <time period>;
3.
has qualifying provisions that have taken legal effect, or by their express terms apply to compensation for work

performed, on or before the end of <time period>;
4.
has qualifying provisions that have not been stayed, enjoined, suspended, invalidated, rescinded, or superseded

as of the Expiration Date at the Expiration time; and
5.
satisfies the Net Monthly Cost test described below.
Subject to the foregoing requirements, an instrument is a Qualifying Action whether its relief is partial or complete,

temporary or permanent, retroactive or prospective, and regardless of its label, vehicle, or stated duration.
Net Monthly Cost test.
An instrument satisfies the Net Monthly Cost test if the Net Monthly Cost under the

instrument does not exceed the monthly minimum wage applicable to sheepherders under California Labor Code

Section 2695.2 and Section 4(E) of Industrial Welfare Commission Wage Order No. 14-2001, plus 15%, as in effect

on the last day of <time period>. An instrument that enjoins or prohibits the enforcement or collection of the

applicable minimum wage and overtime obligations in their entirety is deemed to satisfy this test.
Net Monthly Cost means the employer's minimum required wage and overtime cost of compensating a goat herder

employed on a regularly scheduled 24-hour shift, seven days per week, for one calendar month, computed under the

wage and overtime rules as modified, limited, or rendered unenforceable by the instrument, minus the monthly value

of any credit, reimbursement, grant, subsidy, payment, or contract price adjustment legally available to the employer

under the instrument.
Where and to the extent the goat herder's compensation is determined under hourly wage and overtime rules, the

[page 3 of 5: text layer]
following defaults apply, except to the extent the instrument itself legally modifies the number of compensable hours,

the applicable hourly wage rate, or the applicable premium pay requirements, in which case the instrument's modified

terms govern: all 24 hours of each shift are treated as compensable; the applicable rate is the California minimum

wage in effect on the last day of <time period>; each workweek consists of 40 hours at the regular rate, 40 hours at

one and one half times the regular rate, and 88 hours at two times the regular rate; and one calendar month equals

52/12 workweeks.
Only benefits available as of right to all qualifying employers, without further appropriation, competitive award,

application ranking, or agency discretion, are included in the computation. A lump sum benefit is prorated over the

period to which it is expressly attributable, and a benefit that cannot be allocated on a per goat herder, per month basis

is not included. An instrument consisting of a written order entered by a California state court or a United States

federal court is tested by computing Net Monthly Cost under the obligations as limited by that instrument.
The legal date of an instrument controls, and not the date on which it is published, posted, or reported. A statute is dated as of

the date it becomes law; a regulation as of final approval by the Office of Administrative Law and filing with the Secretary

of State, or as of another legally controlling adoption date; a wage order as of its stated effective date; an administrative

directive, final order, or formal statewide enforcement position as of its official issuance; an executive order or proclamation

as of its issuance; and a court order as of its entry.
The following do not satisfy the Payout Criterion:
a bill that has not become law, including a bill passed by one or both chambers and a bill vetoed and not overridden;
a proposed regulation, rulemaking notice, petition, or draft policy that has not been finally approved and filed;
the filing or pendency of litigation without a written order of a California state court or a United States federal court;
a nonbinding advisory, an opinion letter that neither binds the issuing body nor expressly states that body's statewide

enforcement position, a staff communication, a frequently-asked-questions page, or a website statement;
a statement, press release, hearing, study, report, recommendation, or political agreement;
an authorization of a future program that requires a further appropriation, implementing legislation, or discretionary

agency approval before relief becomes legally available;
a general appropriation or funding for agriculture, grazing, fire prevention, or vegetation management not expressly

tied to goat herder minimum wage or overtime obligations;
a reenactment limited to the definitional, housing, meal period, safety, communication, transportation, or other non-
wage provisions formerly contained in California Labor Code Sections 2695.3 and 2695.4;
federal legislation and federal executive or administrative action, provided that a written order of a United States

federal court is not excluded by this item;
action by a city, county, fire district, or other local government, unless it implements a qualifying state program;
a private settlement or agreement not entered as a written order of a California state court or a United States federal

court;
and relief consisting solely of a limitation on damages, penalties, or interest, without any of (a) any reduction of

the underlying wage, (b) any reduction of overtime obligation, OR (c) any qualifying payment.
Only actions documented by a Source Agency on or before the Expiration Date at the Expiration time will be considered.

Where the records of the Source Agencies conflict, or where a Source Agency retracts, corrects, or removes information, the

official records of the body that took the action govern.
Examples that would resolve the market to Yes:
<time period> is "August 2026." On August 28, 2026, the Legislature passes and the Governor signs an urgency statute

making goat herders eligible for the alternative monthly wage authorized for sheepherders by Labor Code Section

2695.2, effective immediately. The statute is not stayed, enjoined, suspended, or invalidated as of the Expiration Date

at the Expiration time. The Net Monthly Cost under the alternative monthly wage does not exceed the Net Monthly

Cost test threshold.
<time period> is "September 2026." On September 25, 2026, the Governor signs a bill authorizing employers of goat

[page 4 of 5: text layer]
herders to pay, in lieu of the minimum wage for all hours worked, a monthly wage of no less than $5,200, by its

express terms applicable to compensation for work performed on and after July 1, 2026. The monthly minimum wage

applicable to sheepherders in effect on September 30, 2026 is $4,938.21, so the Net Monthly Cost test threshold is

$5,678.94, and the bill's $5,200 Net Monthly Cost does not exceed it.
<time period> is "Q3 2026." On August 20, 2026, the Industrial Welfare Commission amends and republishes Wage

Order No. 14-2001 to provide that a goat herder employed on a regularly scheduled 24-hour, seven-day-per-week on-
call shift is compensable for eight hours per day, effective on that date. The Net Monthly Cost computed under the

amended wage order does not exceed the Net Monthly Cost test threshold.
<time period> is "2026." On November 10, 2026, a California superior court enters a written order in a certified class

action declaring that goat herders statewide are eligible for the alternative monthly wage framework applicable to

sheepherders under Labor Code Section 2695.2. The order is in effect as of the Expiration Date at the Expiration time.

The Net Monthly Cost under the alternative monthly wage does not exceed the Net Monthly Cost test threshold.
Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:
<time period> is "August 2026." The Senate passes a goat herder wage parity bill on August 25, 2026, but the

Assembly does not act on it, and no such bill becomes law on or before August 31, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On September 15, 2026, the Governor signs a bill appropriating $10,000,000 to the

Department of Forestry and Fire Protection for targeted grazing contracts, and no instrument produces any of the

effects listed above on or before December 31, 2026.
<time period> is "Q3 2026." On August 5, 2026, the Labor Commissioner posts a frequently-asked-questions page on

the Department of Industrial Relations website stating that the office does not currently intend to prioritize

enforcement actions against goat-grazing employers, and no instrument produces any of the effects listed above on or

before September 30, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On September 20, 2026, the Governor signs a bill authorizing employers of goat herders to

pay, in lieu of the minimum wage for all hours worked, a monthly wage of no less than $12,000. The monthly

minimum wage applicable to sheepherders in effect on December 31, 2026 is $4,938.21, so the Net Monthly Cost test

threshold is $5,678.94, and the bill's $12,000 Net Monthly Cost exceeds it. No other instrument produces a qualifying

effect on or before December 31, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On October 2, 2026, a California superior court enters an order in a wage claim brought by

one goat herder against one employer holding that the employer may compensate that goat herder on a monthly basis.

The order is limited to the parties to that individual, non-class case.
Minimum Tick:
The Minimum Tick size for the Contract shall be $0.01.
Position Accountability Level:
The Position Accountability Level for the Contract shall be $25,000 per strike, per

Member.
Last Trading Date:
The Last Trading Date of the Contract will be the same as the Expiration Date. The Last Trading Time

will be the same as the Expiration time.
Settlement Date:
The Settlement Date of the Contract shall be no later than the day after the Expiration Date, unless the

Market Outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1.
Expiration Date:
The latest Expiration Date of the Contract shall be one week after the end of <time period>. If an event

described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2.
Expiration time:
The Expiration time of the Contract shall be 10:00 AM ET.
Settlement Value:
The Settlement Value for this Contract is $1.00.
Expiration Value:
The Expiration Value is the value of the Underlying as documented by the Source Agency on the

Expiration Date at the Expiration time.

[page 5 of 5: text layer]
Contingencies:
Before Settlement, Kalshi may, at its sole discretion, initiate the Market Outcome Review Process pursuant

to Rule 7.1 of the Rulebook. If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date, Kalshi has the right to

determine payouts pursuant to Rule 7.1 in the Rulebook.
APPENDIX B – TRADING PROHIBITIONS
In addition to the general prohibition against trading on material nonpublic information, the Exchange will institute additional

prohibitions for trading the contract. Persons under 18 years of age are not permitted to create Kalshi accounts. The

following individuals will be prohibited from trading:
Members, officers, and employees of the California State Senate and State Assembly, including committee, leadership,

and Rules Committee staff, the Office of Legislative Counsel, the Legislative Analyst's Office, and the Chief Clerk's

and Senate Secretary's offices.
The Governor and the Governor's office legislative-affairs and legal-affairs staff; officers and employees of the

Department of Finance, the Office of Administrative Law, and the Secretary of State personnel responsible for

chaptering enrolled bills.
Officers and employees of the Department of Industrial Relations, the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement and

the Labor Commissioner's office, the Industrial Welfare Commission, the Employment Development Department, the

Department of Food and Agriculture, and the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, in each case where the

individual has authority over or advance knowledge of wage-order or enforcement-policy actions affecting goat

herders.
Lobbyists registered with the California Secretary of State on this subject matter, together with their employers and

clients; officers and staff of the California Farm Bureau Federation, the California Wool Growers Association, the

California Cattlemen's Association, the California Labor Federation, and the United Farm Workers.
Counsel of record, party representatives, named plaintiffs, class representatives, expert witnesses, and court personnel

in any pending or threatened action seeking an order that would satisfy the Payout Criterion.
Any person retained to draft or negotiate proposed statutory or regulatory language on this subject, including officers,

directors, and employees of California goat-grazing and targeted-grazing contractors participating in that drafting or

negotiation.
Immediate family members and members of the household of any person listed above.

Pursuant to Commission Rule 40.2(a)(3)(v), the following is a concise explanation and analysis
of the product and its compliance with the Act, including the relevant Core Principles (discussed
in Appendix D), and the Commission's regulations thereunder.
I. Introduction

The “Will an alternative wage for Californian goat herders be authorized <time period>?”

Further information about the Contract, including an analysis of its risk mitigation and
price basing utility, as well as additional considerations related to the Contract, is
included in Confidential Appendices C, D, and E.

Pursuant to Section 5c(c) of the Act and CFTC Regulations 40.2(a), the Exchange hereby
certifies that the listing of the Contract complies with the Act and Commission
regulations under the Act.

General Contract Terms and Conditions: The Contract operates similar to other event
contracts that the Exchange lists for trading. The minimum price fluctuation is $0.01 (one
cent). Price bands will apply so that Contracts may only be listed at values of at least
$0.01 and at most $0.99. Further, the Contract is sized with a one-dollar notional value
and has a minimum price fluctuation of $0.01 to enable Members to match the size of the
contracts purchased to their economic risks. As outlined in Rule 5.16 of the Rulebook,
trading shall be available at all times outside of any maintenance windows, which will be
announced in advance by the Exchange. Members will be charged fees in accordance
with Rule 3.13 of the Rulebook. Fees, if they are charged, are charged in such amounts as
may be revised from time to time to be reflected on the Exchange’s Website. A new
Source Agency can be added via a Part 40 amendment. All instructions on how to access

the Underlying are non-binding and are provided for convenience only and are not part of
the binding Terms and Conditions of the Contract. They may be clarified at any time.
Furthermore, the Contract’s payout structure is characterized by the payment of an
absolute amount to the holder of one side of the option and no payment to the
counterparty. During the time that trading on the Contract is open, Members are able to
adjust their positions and trade freely. The Expiration Value and Market Outcome are
determined at or after Market Close. The market is then settled by the Exchange, and the
long position holders and short position holders are paid according to the Market
Outcome. In this case, “long position holders” refers to Members who purchased the
“Yes” side of the Contract and “short position holders” refers to Members who purchased
the “No” side of the Contract. If the Market Outcome is “Yes,” meaning that an event
occurs that is encompassed within the Payout Criterion, then the long position holders are
paid an absolute amount proportional to the size of their position and the short position
holders receive no payment. If the Market Outcome is “No,” then the short position
holders are paid an absolute amount proportional to the size of their position and the long
position holders receive no payment. Specification of the circumstances that would
trigger a Market Outcome of “Yes” are included below in the section titled “Payout
Criterion” in Appendix A.

At.description: The condition holds at the instant `at` (spec §4).
At.title: At

By.description:
The condition holds at some observation up to the deadline, which is included or not as `closed` says (spec §4
"By(expr, t)"; A05 §5.4 endpoint inclusion). `since` is the earliest observation that counts, with its own
inclusion, or None where every earlier observation counts: the sources give By no lower bound, so the contract
states it (ours).
By.title: By

Category.description: A category or text value, compared as given.
Category.title: Category

Cmp.description:
observable op value, at the instant or day its enclosing temporal operator gives (spec §4). The value's type is
the observable's (`VALUE_KIND`); a numeric value is compared at the observable's declared precision (A09 §10.3).
Cmp.title: Cmp

Computed.description:
A number computed by a registered consequence node from numeric sub-expressions (spec §5: "The contract IR
compiles into the computation layer, so the settlement function and the hedge payoff are the same code"; I7: code
owns consequences). The node is pure and registered (spec §4 @node), so the same arithmetic settles, prices and
fuzzes; over interval inputs its value is the interval of its outputs.
Computed.title: Computed

ConflictPolicy.description:
How disagreeing sources are reconciled: a registered procedure and its parameters (A05 §5.4: "Use a registered
procedure ID plus parameters, or an explicit typed policy"). The two procedures registered so far are ours, the
two readings of spec §4's precedence list that an evaluator can apply deterministically: precedence_first_available,
the highest-ranked source in the procedure's precedence that has published settles; require_agreement, the sources
named in `sources` must agree, or the result is disputed. A contract whose rule is neither is not supported exactly
(A05 §5.5) until its procedure is registered here.
ConflictPolicy.title: ConflictPolicy

ContractIR.description: A contract in the IR (spec §4). Every observable the trigger or payout references is declared.
ContractIR.title: ContractIR

CountTrue.description:
The number of calendar days of `days` on which the condition holds, counted in the window's time zone (spec §4).
Its value over three-valued days is an interval [k, k + u] (A05 §5.3).
CountTrue.title: CountTrue

DurationIn.description:
The time within the window during which the condition holds, in `unit` (spec §4); an interval over unknowns, as
CountTrue's is. calendar_day counts calendar days of the window's time zone; elapsed_day counts 24-hour periods, so
a daylight-saving change does not change it (A05 §5.4: "Define ... day-count conventions").
DurationIn.title: DurationIn

Exclusion.description:
An exclusion clause. One that changes settlement is operative and names the IR or interpretive node that carries
it; a disclosure note is marked non-operative (A05 §5.4).
Exclusion.title: Exclusion

Interpretive.description:
A condition a resolver must judge from text (spec §4): a question template and its bindings, answered by decision
models and mapped to a truth by its answer's status (spec §6.3).
Interpretive.title: Interpretive

ListingBinding.description:
One per-market listing field of a series and the IR value it fills (ours; spec §9.3's per-market fields). `field`
is the market record's field, a dotted path into its objects where the value is nested (custom_strike.Option).
`node` and `slot` name the value it fills: a node's threshold (Cmp, NumCmp), the instant it reads (At, ValueAt), a
By's bounds (since, deadline), or a window's ends (Throughout, CountTrue, DurationIn); or, with no node, one of the
timing's dates (open, close, expiration, observation_cutoff). The field's value enters as it is, in the slot's type:
a threshold takes the number, text or date its comparison's value is, an instant slot an instant.
ListingBinding.title: ListingBinding

NumCmp.description:
A count or duration compared with a threshold, e.g. CountTrue(...) >= 20 (ours: spec §4 puts CountTrue and
DurationIn in the Expr union, and a trigger on them, such as spec §2.5's "how many days ... will station S record at
least X inches", compares their value).
NumCmp.title: NumCmp

Observable.description:
A quantity a contract settles on (spec §4).

revision_policy: which vintage settles (spec §4). "final" is a finite rule only with a declared resolution deadline
or a fallback (addendum A05 §5.4: "An unlimited `final` vintage is not a finite settlement rule unless 'final' has a
declared resolution deadline or fallback"): `final_deadline` is the instant by which the value must be final, and
`final_fallback` the vintage that settles if no final value is published by the settlement determination. unit and precision: what a numeric value is measured in and the precision at which it is published
(A05 §5.4 unit conversions; A09 §10.3 thresholds at declared precision).
Observable.title: Observable

Payout.description:
Per unit (spec §4). currency, and rounding to `rounding_quantum` by `rounding_mode`, are explicit (A05 §5.1,
§5.4: "Define ... rounding"). payment: paid once at settlement, or per
period of `periods`, each period's amount paid after its end (A05 §5.3: "A count paid once at expiry and a strip paid
periodically can have identical terminal amounts and very different liquidity consequences").
Payout.title: Payout

ReadValue.description:
A number a resolver reads from text, with its unit: a term an instrument sets (an alternative monthly wage, a
modified overtime threshold). Decision models answer it as a closed set of bands (spec §4: a question answered by a
distribution over a closed set), so its value is the interval of the band the resolved answer names, and unknown is
the whole range (A05 §5.3: a number left open by unknowns is an interval, never a guess). Each band is [low, high),
the last [low, high], so a value on a shared endpoint belongs to the band above it (A05 §5.4: "Define open/closed
interval endpoints"). Ours: spec §9.3's specimen tests a cost computed from such terms, and spec §4's Interpretive
yields only a truth.
ReadValue.title: ReadValue

Ref.description: A versioned reference to another record or policy (addendum §5.1 VersionedRef).
Ref.title: Ref

ResolutionProcedure.description:
How the contract resolves (spec §4, amended by A05 §5.2 and §5.4). on_unknown_at_expiry says what an unknown
trigger means at settlement without changing the trigger's truth (A05 §5.2). early_expiration: "when_true" when the
contract expires early once its trigger is true (spec §9.3: "early_close_condition"; the Western Grazers terms: "If
an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance
with Rule 7.2"). Its timing is what the contract states: "first_true" where the contract itself fixes the instant at
which the trigger is first true on the observations then published; "per_exchange_rule" where it defers to a rule
outside the IR's sources, named in early_expiration_rule, and then the outcome is determined once the trigger is
true while the early date stays unresolved, named, until that rule is supplied (A05 §5.2: "Unsupported procedure
details must be reported, not guessed"). An extension names its length and what happens if the trigger is still
unknown after it.
ResolutionProcedure.title: ResolutionProcedure

ScenarioExample.description:
A published example: a scenario that passed fuzzing, with the evaluator's outcome (spec §8.5, I8). `evaluation`
is the content hash of the ResolutionEvaluation that produced `expected`.
ScenarioExample.title: ScenarioExample

SettlementBinding.description:
What a market record's settlement value reports (ours; spec §9.3: "settled markets supplying known outcomes"):
the observable whose value the exchange settled on, and the market field (`at_field`) giving the instant that value
is for.
SettlementBinding.title: SettlementBinding

Source.description: A source of an observable's values, ranked by authority (spec §4: rank 1 is highest).
Source.title: Source

Throughout.description: The condition holds at every observation in the window (spec §4).
Throughout.title: Throughout

TimeWindow.description:
A window of time (spec §4), with each endpoint's inclusion stated (addendum A05 §5.4: "Define open/closed interval
endpoints, timezone"). `tz` is the IANA zone in which calendar days of the window are counted.
TimeWindow.title: TimeWindow

Timing.description:
The contract's dates (spec §4), with the cutoff for observations and the payment lag distinguished from the
settlement determination (A05 §5.3: event, publication, observation cutoff, settlement determination and payment
dates are different dates). Lags count calendar days or business days, in the time zone `tz` (A05 §5.4: "Define ...
timezone, day-count conventions"); a business-day lag skips weekends and the holidays of `holiday_calendar`, whose
one registered calendar is the United States federal holidays of 5 U.S.C. §6103 (ours: the calendar the contracts
we build settle against; another is registered here before a contract can use it, A05 §5.4 "Mechanical policies
must be executable").
Timing.title: Timing

ValueAt.description:
A numeric observable's value at an instant, selected by the contract's revision and conflict policies (spec §4
Observable; ours: a computed test reads published rates, such as a minimum wage in effect on a day).
ValueAt.title: ValueAt

VoidTransfer.description: What a void returns per unit (A05 §5.2: "A void result does not imply a particular refund").
VoidTransfer.title: VoidTransfer

schema.description:
contract_reader: a filed series read into the IR as an instrument family (core.ContractFamily's fields that are
the reader's): the support classification with its assumptions and unsupported terms (core.HarvestedContract), the
representative market's IR (its id and version are code's), the bindings that say which IR value each per-market
listing field fills (core.ListingBinding), and what a market record's settlement value reports
(core.SettlementBinding). Validated as the core family it drafts, so an answer the definition refuses is refused
here, with the definition's reasons.
schema.title: HarvestDraft

request.system:
You read a listed event contract series' filed terms into Requisite's contract IR, a formal representation that one evaluator settles in three-valued logic. A series is one set of filed terms listed as many markets that differ only in their listing fields (a strike, their times, the event). You read it as an instrument family: one representative market's IR, and bindings that say which IR value each per-market listing field fills, from which code gives every market its IR. Code validates and tests what you propose; you only propose.

You are given:
- series: the exchange's series record.
- filings: the filed documents' text as extracted from their PDFs (the contract terms, and the product certification where there is one), with anything that could not be read.
- representative_market: the listing fields of the market whose IR you write.
- markets: how many markets the series has, their tickers, and each listing field whose value varies across them, with its number of distinct values and its values at a few markets.
- listing_fields: the market fields a binding may read.
You are not shown how any market settled, nor any price. Your IRs are checked afterwards against how the settled markets settled.

Produce:
- support: "supported_exact" when the IR carries every operative term as filed; "supported_with_explicit_assumptions" when it carries them only under assumptions you list; "unsupported" when a term that decides settlement cannot be expressed, which you name in unsupported_terms. Never simplify a term silently: a term you could not carry exactly is an assumption or an unsupported term, stated in the filing's own words.
- ir: the representative market's contract in the IR, or null when unsupported. Code sets its id and version.
- bindings: for each listing field that varies across the markets and that the IR depends on, the IR value it fills: field, node, slot. A slot is a node's "threshold" (Cmp, NumCmp), the instant a node reads ("at": At, ValueAt), a By's "since" or "deadline", a window's "window_start" or "window_end" (Throughout, CountTrue, DurationIn), or, with node null, one of the timing's dates ("open", "close", "expiration", "observation_cutoff"). field is one of listing_fields, a dotted path where the value is nested (custom_strike.<key>). The field's value fills the slot exactly as listed, in the slot's type: a number fills a number threshold, a text a text threshold, a timestamp an instant. Write the representative IR with the representative market's own values in every bound slot; code checks that the bindings reproduce it from that market's record. No bindings when unsupported.
- settlement: what a market's settlement value reports. The exchange's record of a settled market states "the value that was considered for the settlement"; name the IR observable whose value that is, and the listing field giving the instant that value is for, the instant the IR reads it at. null where the settlement value is no observable of the IR (for instance, the outcome of a criterion a resolver judges from text), or when unsupported.

How to read the terms into the IR:
- Observables are the quantities the terms settle on (a published value, a status, a date), each with the sources the terms name, ranked as the terms rank them, its revision policy as the terms state it, and for a number its unit and published precision.
- The trigger is the payout criterion. Mechanical conditions (a value compared with a threshold, a count of days, a date before a deadline) are Cmp, NumCmp, By, At, Throughout, CountTrue or DurationIn over observables. Anything a resolver must judge from text (whether an instrument qualifies, whether its effect meets a description, whether it is in effect) is an Interpretive node: a question template name and its bindings, stating the condition in the filing's words. A number a resolver must read from text is a ReadValue with bands; a computation the terms define is a Computed node naming a consequence function and its inputs.
- The comparison, and whether its bound is included, come from the filed terms and the market's rules text, never from a field's name; a strike field supplies only the value.
- Every node has an id, unique in the contract, short and descriptive.
- Timing, the resolution procedure (source precedence, conflict rule, what an unknown at expiry means, early expiration and its timing, extensions, voids) and the payout follow the terms exactly. Where the terms defer to an exchange rule outside the filing, name the rule (early_expiration_rule) rather than inventing its content. Where a date depends on events (an expiration that is the sooner of when data is available and a latest date), state the date the IR takes as an assumption, quoting the term.
- Exclusions that change settlement are operative and name the node that carries them; disclosure notes are not.

Read the terms whole before writing anything. Where the terms are ambiguous, do not resolve the ambiguity in the IR: list it as an assumption with both readings.

Where carrying a term exactly needs a construct the IR does not have, never approximate it silently. Either list it as
an assumption, giving the filing's words and how the IR carries them instead, or, when it decides settlement and no
faithful carriage exists, name it as an unsupported term. Constructs the IR is known not to have:
- a condition quantified over documents ("any instrument that ...", "a qualifying action"), where the IR can only
  read one named instrument;
- a reading whose answer is a single value other than the top of its range (bands are [low, high));
- a date read from text and compared;
- a source hierarchy for the evidence behind an interpretive condition, as distinct from an observable's sources;
- an unknown-at-expiry outcome left to the exchange's discretion;
- a settlement or payment date stated as a deadline ("no later than");
- a known payment whose date is left to an exchange rule;
- a missing-data rule for a payout quantity;
- what a binary or capped payout pays per period;
- an early expiration when the outcome is decided either way (the IR expires early only when its trigger is true).
Where the IR requires a field the terms do not state (a void transfer with no void path, a rounding mode), give the
neutral value and list it as an assumption that the terms state no such rule.

unsupported_terms: Payout Criterion quantified over documents: "The Payout Criterion for the Contract encompasses the Expiration Values that a Qualifying Action has been taken <time period>." A Qualifying Action is any instrument in five open classes: "a California statute has become law ...", "a regulation finally approved ...", "a written regulation, binding directive, final order, or formal statewide enforcement policy issued by a California state agency ...", "an executive order or proclamation ...", or "a written order entered by a California state court or a United States federal court". Each must also have one of six listed effects and pass five conditions. The IR can only read one named instrument, and no instrument is named. This term decides settlement.

Net Monthly Cost test, run on each instrument: "An instrument satisfies the Net Monthly Cost test if the Net Monthly Cost under the instrument does not exceed the monthly minimum wage applicable to sheepherders under California Labor Code Section 2695.2 and Section 4(E) of Industrial Welfare Commission Wage Order No. 14-2001, plus 15%, as in effect on the last day of <time period>." The Net Monthly Cost is "computed under the wage and overtime rules as modified, limited, or rendered unenforceable by the instrument, minus the monthly value of any credit, reimbursement, grant, subsidy, payment, or contract price adjustment legally available to the employer under the instrument". It uses default hours, rates and premiums "except to the extent the instrument itself legally modifies" them, and the deemed-satisfaction rule "An instrument that enjoins or prohibits the enforcement or collection of the applicable minimum wage and overtime obligations in their entirety is deemed to satisfy this test." The Computed and ReadValue inputs would have to be read from whichever instrument is found to qualify. The IR cannot bind them to an instrument that is not named, and its bands cannot give a single value read from text, such as a stated monthly wage of "no less than $5,200".

Dates read from text and compared: the instrument "was enacted, approved and filed, issued, or entered, as applicable, on or before the end of <time period>" and "has qualifying provisions that have taken legal effect, or by their express terms apply to compensation for work performed, on or before the end of <time period>". Under the legal-date rules ("The legal date of an instrument controls, and not the date on which it is published, posted, or reported ..."), these dates are read from each instrument's text.

Source hierarchy for the evidence behind the interpretive condition: "Where the records of the Source Agencies conflict, or where a Source Agency retracts, corrects, or removes information, the official records of the body that took the action govern." This applies on top of the ranked list of Source Agencies (California Legislative Information first, Fox News last). It governs the evidence for the qualifying-action judgment, not the value of a published observable.

Outcome when the result is unknown at expiry is left to the exchange: "If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date, Kalshi has the right to determine payouts pursuant to Rule 7.1 in the Rulebook."
Settlement date stated as a deadline: "The Settlement Date of the Contract shall be no later than the day after the Expiration Date, unless the Market Outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1."
